statusText: Tail rises to 23%. Mapped policy state: WATCH. The 31,196.75 low that had held for three hours gave way and NQ Dec26 printed a new 31,120.00 session low, trading 31,157.00 at -0.78%. A record week of Strait of Hormuz tanker strikes has pushed Brent near 105 and WTI near 92.6, both around +4.9%, while VIX at 15.99 sits near its session high and the 10-year yield holds 5.35% around a 24-year high. Tail stays below the 25% blocking threshold because the break extended rather than accelerated.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is WATCH with Tail at 23%, inside the 20-24% band and below the 25% blocking threshold. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 12:30Z-16:00Z, spanning the jobless-claims print, the U.S. cash open and the first cash hours, where conditional Tail peaks at 26% and maps to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Conditional Tail eases to 22% by the 16:00Z window close, lifts to 23% across the 17:00Z 30-year auction and the 17:40Z Fed Musalem speech, and returns to the EA_ON band from 20:00Z as the cash session completes. Stress at 65% enters the high band and is the dominant reading: the environment is difficult and may still mean-revert. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active throughout.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures break a three-hour base to a new session low as record Hormuz tanker strikes lift Brent near 105 and the 10-year yield holds a 24-year high
body:
The twelfth Globex hour of the Oct 7-8 session resolved the base downward. NQ Dec26 traded 31,157.00 as of 11:16:46Z, -245.25 or -0.78% against a 31,402.25 prior close, corroborated independently at 31,158.75 with a matching -0.78%. The session range widened to 31,119.75-31,466.00, worth 346 points or 1.10%, as the 31,196.75 low that had held for three consecutive hours gave way to a new 31,120.00 low. Reuters reported Nasdaq-100 e-minis at -180.25 or -0.57% at 10:14Z, so the move has deepened by roughly a fifth of a percent in the hour since. That is a genuine structural break rather than the consolidation published an hour ago.

What holds Tail at 23% rather than through the 25% blocking threshold is how the break has behaved. Price trades about 37 points above the new low, so the first move after the breakdown was a modest bounce and not immediate extension. The day's loss is 0.78%, which is an orderly repricing rather than violent directional discovery, and VIX at 15.99 is historically low in absolute terms even after rising 6.04% into a 15.31-16.02 range. A sub-16 VIX is not the volatility signature of a sustained no-retracement path. Under the inherited contract this is an amplifier stack that has not yet produced the repeated extension after failed retracements that defines a pathological price path.

The amplifiers themselves are real and newly stronger. CNN reported that Kpler counted 10 tankers struck in the Strait of Hormuz between September 28 and October 4, a record well above the previous weekly high of six, with a tanker hit by multiple projectiles on Wednesday causing casualties and only seven tankers transiting on Tuesday, the fewest since July 23. Brent rose 4.3% to about 104.48 early Thursday and is quoted near 105.07, with WTI near 92.05-92.68 at about +4.9%. Hurricane Isaias is approaching the U.S. Gulf refining hub, with Shell and Chevron curtailing production. European gas and diesel have followed, ICE Gasoil closing up 6% on Wednesday, feeding a renewed European bond selloff. Treasury yields are aligned: 2-year 4.82%, 10-year 5.35% around a 24-year high though below earlier session highs, and 30-year 5.72%.

Index internals conflict rather than confirm. Semiconductors were weaker in pre-market trade with Nvidia -0.6%, Broadcom -1.4% and Micron -1.2%, even as Samsung forecast a record quarterly profit. A Wall Street Journal report that Broadcom is lining up $50 billion of financing for OpenAI, with Oracle also seeking funds, has raised concern about heavy technology debt issuance competing for capital at these yields. Dow e-minis at -0.78% and S&P e-minis at -0.4% place Nasdaq-100 in the middle of the complex rather than leading a tech-specific break, which argues against a Nasdaq-100-specific one-way path.

Policy is a standing conflict rather than a fresh shock. Fed Governor Waller, speaking at 08:30Z, hinted at a possible pause at the upcoming meeting while saying more hikes would likely be needed to reach 2% inflation, with the pace retaining flexibility. CME FedWatch has an October hold widely expected and a December hike still possible. Initial and continuing jobless claims have not yet printed at this assessment time and are scheduled for 12:30Z; no actual is published or assumed here. Before the release, hypothetical post-event alignment is not counted as observed, which is why the conditional 26% peak sits in the forecast rather than in the current score.

Stress rises to 65% and enters the high band. That is the honest reading of this environment: an energy supply shock, a long end at generational highs, a European bond selloff and a broken intraday base together make for a difficult, high-volatility tape that can still mean-revert. Confidence holds at 88% on two independent live NQ quotes, live VIX, a primary yield aggregator, two independent oil sources, dated Reuters session reporting and a verified forward calendar. The shared Finviz context file was read and is dated 2026-09-29 with partial collection status, roughly nine days old and far outside the 90-minute freshness contract, so it was treated as stale and contributed nothing to this assessment; publication proceeded on independent research as the contract requires.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. Tail opened the window at 21% in a trend-down phase that peaked at 23% into the Oct 7 U.S. cash open, then decayed steadily once that dip was retraced: every hour from 16:00Z on Oct 7 through 05:00Z on Oct 8 held the 10-18% EA_ON band with Stress at 47-53%. The final four hours trace the current episode. Tail lifted to 14% at 06:00Z as the 05:16Z retracement failed, jumped to 22% at 07:00Z when a second failed retracement set the 31,196.75 low, then held a 20% WATCH floor through 08:00Z, 09:00Z and 10:00Z while that low was defended and the range stayed unchanged. Stress climbed monotonically across those same four hours from 55% to 62% as oil and yields built, which is precisely the divergence the contract expects: a deteriorating environment registering in Stress while Tail waited for structural confirmation. This hour supplies that confirmation with the break of the low, lifting Tail to 23%.
outlookSummary: Base case is that the break of 31,196.75 to a new 31,120.00 low is a range expansion into a difficult inflation-shock tape rather than the opening of a sustained one-way path, with two-way rotation resuming once the U.S. cash auction prices the Hormuz supply shock and the long end. Record Strait of Hormuz tanker strikes, Brent near 105, a 10-year yield at 5.35% around a 24-year high, a renewed euro-area bond selloff and a confirmed Fed hiking bias remain the dominant background conflict. Conditional Tail holds 24% across the 12:30Z claims print, peaks at 26% through the 13:30Z cash open and the first full cash hour where an already-aligned bearish regime meeting the opening auction is the specific mean-reversion-failure pattern, then eases to 22% by the 16:00Z close of the published 12:30Z-16:00Z danger window. A secondary 23% checkpoint spans the 17:00Z 30-year auction and the 17:40Z Fed Musalem speech, since yields lead this tape. Conditional Tail returns to the EA_ON band at 20:00Z and troughs at 12% in the Asia-to-Europe handover before lifting to 17% by the end of the horizon on widening forecast uncertainty. Invalidation of the base case would be repeated extension after failed retracements with price pinned near the lows through the cash open; confirmation would be a retracement into the 31,300s.

forecastDetail.comment: Current hour, observed: the three-hour base at 31,196.75 failed and a new 31,120.00 session low printed, with NQ Dec26 at 31,157.00, -0.78%. The break extended rather than accelerated, price holding about 37 points above the low, so Tail rises one point to 23% and remains below the 25% blocking threshold. Mapped policy state: WATCH.

Contains the 12:30Z jobless-claims print. Conditional Tail holds the 24% top of the WATCH band on the assumption the broken base stays unrepaired; a reclaim of 31,196.75 before the release would argue the other way. Stress 66% reflects the oil and long-end shock, not the release itself.

Contains the 13:30Z U.S. cash open and is the joint peak at a conditional 26%, mapping to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. The reasoning is pattern-specific: an already-aligned bearish regime meeting the opening auction is the structure that has previously denied mean reversion. A two-way auction retracing into the 31,300s would invalidate it.

First full cash hour, holding the conditional 26% peak with 14:00Z wholesale inventories a minor checkpoint. The mechanism carried here is a second leg extending after a failed retracement; rotation contained inside the opening range retires it. Tech-debt supply concerns add background pressure.

Post-open digestion. Conditional Tail steps back to 24% inside the WATCH band on the base case that the cash auction establishes two-way trade, while Stress holds 66% because an oil-and-yield inflation shock does not resolve inside one session.

Closes the published 12:30Z-16:00Z danger window. Conditional Tail eases to 22% on the assumption no persistent one-way structure was established through the open, and Stress returns to the elevated band at 64% as European cash trade winds down.
